topic: Plant Growth: Phases, Rates and Conditions
title: How Do Plants Grow? Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
A maize root tip makes more than 17,500 new cells an hour, and a mango tree keeps growing all its life. Aarav measures a bean seedling every day and asks: how do we measure growth, and does a plant grow by the same amount each day?

We see what growth is and how it is measured, zoom from a root to its tip to its cells to find the meristematic, elongation and maturation phases, watch arithmetic growth draw a straight line and geometric growth draw a sigmoid curve, compare absolute and relative growth rates, and list the conditions growth needs with a pause and think. Then a worked example with leaves A and B, the exam trap, an original NEET pattern statement question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 91 of our PUC Biology series.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE), PUC (Karnataka) and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 How fast does a root tip grow?
0:40 What is growth?
1:10 Zoom ladder: root, root tip, cells
1:38 Arithmetic vs geometric growth
2:38 Absolute vs relative growth rate
2:53 Conditions for growth + pause and think
3:45 Worked example: leaves A and B
4:11 Exam trap: does geometric growth rise forever?
4:32 Practice question (NEET pattern)
5:07 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Differentiation, Dedifferentiation and Redifferentiation. How can a cell that stopped dividing long ago start dividing again?
